name: Bishop's Lodge, Auberge Collection
positioning: Historic Southwestern mountain resort in the foothills of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, bordering national forest near Santa Fe
best_for: Travelers who want a Santa Fe base with mountain scenery and a shuttle to the downtown plaza
Couples and families wanting kiva-fireplace rooms, casitas or the Bunkhouse

facts.text: Bishop's Lodge sits in the foothills of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains near Santa Fe and borders 1.7 million acres of national forest.
The lodge's chapel was built in 1874 as a private retreat by Jean-Baptiste Lamy, the first Roman Catholic archbishop of Santa Fe.
The chapel later became the centerpiece of the original Bishop's Lodge, which dates to 1918.
Guestrooms have private terraces, traditional kiva fireplaces and woven Navajo rugs.
The Kiva Suites are mountaintop suites with an outdoor plunge pool.
The Bunkhouse is crafted from reclaimed barn wood.
The restaurant SkyFire draws inspiration from ingredients and textures found in Mexico.
SkyFire offers dishes created in collaboration with Deborah Davis, author of The Art of Canine Cuisine.
Hotel guests have an outdoor pool and hot tub.
The spa, Stream Dance, Wellbeing by Auberge, has its treatments in a casita-style adobe building.
A complimentary shuttle runs to the Santa Fe downtown plaza.
Guests may borrow a complimentary Mercedes-Benz test vehicle to explore Santa Fe and the surrounding area.

highlights.text: The chapel was built in 1874 as a private retreat by Santa Fe's first Roman Catholic archbishop and later became the centerpiece of the original lodge.
The Kiva Suites sit on the mountaintop and have an outdoor plunge pool.
SkyFire cooks with wood and draws on Mexican ingredients and textures.
SkyFire has dishes made for dogs, created with the author of The Art of Canine Cuisine.
Guests can borrow a complimentary Mercedes-Benz test vehicle for up to four hours, subject to availability.

considerations.text: WhataHotel notes a location outside downtown Santa Fe.
The lodge is about 20 minutes from Santa Fe Regional Airport and 75 minutes from Albuquerque International Sunport.
The downtown plaza shuttle is first come, first served, and the Mercedes-Benz test vehicle is subject to availability.
